messages:
Marco (Marketing): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands: can leadership confirm the short positioning line we should use for partner decks? @Claire @Raj
Claire (CEO): Use: 'Production-grade inference that makes cost, latency, and reliability predictable.' Keep partner decks focused on outcomes, not infra details.
Tess (Field Engineer): Partners ask how we differ from simple managed endpoints. Need a single sentence for partner-facing docs.
Raj (VP Product): Suggested line: 'We combine a high-performance inference runtime with rollout controls and transparent cost telemetry so teams can ship reliably.' Neutral; avoids vendor names.
Marco (Marketing): Good. For partner enablement, should we include a short note about Dedicated vs Private? Partners want clarity on compliance customers.
Claire (CEO): One-liner: 'Dedicated = reserved capacity with SLAs; Private = customer-managed networking or on-prem for regulated workloads.'
Tess (Field Engineer): Ops note: SRE asked us to be clear about fallbacks in partner docs. Can we confirm fallback behavior?
Raj (VP Product): Confirmed: policy-based routing -> canary -> primary -> configured fallback (hosted or compatible variant). We'll publish a one-page summary in docs soon.
Marco (Marketing): Timeline: when can partners expect updated deck text and a short handout?
Claire (CEO): Updated partner wording in 8 business days. Handout + one-pager on fallbacks in 3 weeks.
ops-bot: Slides uploaded: https://redwood-inference.slides/ah-2054445555 :page_facing_up:
Marco (Marketing): Thanks all. I'll post drafts to #partners for review.
thread_text_summary: Follow-up clarifying partner-facing one-liners: core positioning, neutral competitor phrasing, Dedicated vs Private differentiation, fallback behavior summary, and timelines for partner deck updates.
